# NIS2 scoping rules, as written

<!-- GENERATED by the Reglyze repository's corpus build (tools/corpus-export/build-corpus.mjs); edit the sources, not this file. -->

Every statement below is quoted and sourced in [legal-sources/eu.md](../legal-sources/eu.md)
(Directive (EU) 2022/2555, OJ L 333; Recommendation 2003/361/EC, OJ L 124) and in
[legal-sources/slovenia.md](../legal-sources/slovenia.md) (ZInfV-1, Uradni list RS, št. 40/2025).
The machine-readable cases are in [scoping-conformance-cases.json](scoping-conformance-cases.json);
a classifier that returns the expected verdict for every case reads the texts the way they are written.

## 1. Size (Recommendation 2003/361/EC, Annex, Article 2)

The headcount ceiling is mandatory. Of the two financial ceilings an enterprise only has to
respect **one**: the text reads "annual turnover ... **and/or** ... annual balance sheet total".
Staff limits are strict ("fewer than"), money limits inclusive ("not exceeding").

| category | condition |
|---|---|
| small | staff < 50 **and** (turnover ≤ EUR 10M **or** balance sheet ≤ EUR 10M) |
| medium (NIS2 Art. 2(1) applies) | not small, **and** staff < 250 **and** (turnover ≤ EUR 50M **or** balance sheet ≤ EUR 43M) |
| exceeds the medium ceilings ("large") | staff ≥ 250 **or** (turnover > EUR 50M **and** balance sheet > EUR 43M) |

Two consequences that tools get wrong: a 30-person company with EUR 12M turnover and a EUR 5M
balance sheet is small; a 100-person company with EUR 60M turnover and a EUR 30M balance sheet is
medium. Partner and linked enterprises are aggregated (Annex Art. 6); a status changes only after
two consecutive accounting periods (Annex Art. 4(2)).

## 2. In scope regardless of size (Directive Article 2(2) to 2(4))

Article 2(2)(a) is a **closed list**: providers of public electronic communications networks or of
publicly available electronic communications services; trust service providers; top-level domain
name registries and DNS service providers. **Cloud computing, data centre, content delivery network,
internet exchange point, managed service and managed security service providers are not in it**:
they are Annex I activities subject to the size test. Also regardless of size: entities a Member
State identifies under Article 2(2)(b) to (e); central-government public administration
(2(2)(f)(i)); regional public administration that a Member State's risk-based assessment brings in
(2(2)(f)(ii)); critical entities under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 (2(3)); entities providing domain
name registration services (2(4), in scope but in neither class).

## 3. Essential versus important (Directive Article 3)

Essential (Art. 3(1)): (a) Annex I types that exceed the medium ceilings; (b) qualified trust
service providers, TLD registries and DNS providers regardless of size; (c) providers of public
electronic communications that qualify as **medium-sized** enterprises; (d) central-government
public administration; (e) entities a Member State identified as essential; (f) critical entities;
(g) former operators of essential services where the Member State so provides. Every other in-scope
Annex I or II entity is important (Art. 3(2)): a medium-sized Annex I entity is important, a small
public e-communications provider is important, a non-qualified trust service provider is important
unless it is large.

## 4. A national test that departs from the Recommendation: Slovenia

ZInfV-1 Art. 6(1) is **cumulative**: an Annex 1 or 2 entity is obliged if it has at least 50
employees **and** an annual turnover or balance sheet total of at least EUR 10 million (inclusive,
"vsaj"). Art. 7(2) pt 1 makes the essential test **disjunctive**: at least 250 employees **or**
turnover of at least EUR 50 million **or** a balance sheet total of at least EUR 43 million, for
entities that pass the general test. Public e-communications providers are essential from 50
employees and EUR 10 million (Art. 7(2) pt 3), important below (Art. 7(3)); state-level
administration is essential (Art. 7(2) pt 4), urban municipalities are important (Art. 6(3) pt 4,
Art. 7(3)).

## 5. Not modelled

Domain-name registrars (Art. 2(4)), critical entities under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 (Art. 2(3)),
the aggregation of partner and linked enterprises (Recommendation Annex Art. 6), Member-State
extensions to local administration (Art. 2(5)) and national sector rules such as the Polish MSSP
rule (UKSC art. 5 ust. 1 pkt 3) are outside the suite. A classifier that handles them goes beyond
it, not against it.

| id | country | case | expected | basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| size-01 | DE | 18 employees, EUR 2.6M turnover, EUR 2M balance sheet, manufacturing | out_of_scope | Small enterprise: fewer than 50 staff and turnover not exceeding EUR 10M (Recommendation Annex Art. 2(2)); outside Directive Art. 2(1). |
| size-02 | DE | 30 employees, EUR 12M turnover, EUR 5M balance sheet, manufacturing | out_of_scope | Still small: the balance sheet does not exceed EUR 10M and one financial ceiling suffices (the Annex says 'and/or'). |
| size-03 | DE | 30 employees, EUR 12M turnover, EUR 12M balance sheet, manufacturing | important | Not small: both financial ceilings exceeded; an Annex II medium enterprise is an important entity (Art. 3(2)). |
| size-04 | DE | 50 employees, EUR 9M turnover, EUR 8M balance sheet, manufacturing | important | Headcount alone makes it medium: 'fewer than 50 persons' is the small ceiling (Recommendation Annex Art. 2(2)). |
| size-05 | DE | 100 employees, EUR 60M turnover, EUR 30M balance sheet, energy | important | Does not exceed the medium ceilings: that needs 250 staff, or turnover above 50M and a balance sheet above 43M (Recommendation Annex Art. 2(1)); an Annex I medium enterprise is important (Art. 3(2)). |
| size-06 | DE | 100 employees, EUR 60M turnover, EUR 44M balance sheet, energy | essential | Exceeds the medium ceilings on both financial limbs; a large Annex I entity is essential (Art. 3(1)(a)). |
| size-07 | DE | 250 employees, EUR 3M turnover, EUR 2M balance sheet, manufacturing | important | 250 staff exceeds the medium ceilings, but Art. 3(1)(a) covers Annex I only; a large Annex II entity is important (Art. 3(2)). |
| size-08 | DE | 300 employees, EUR 5M turnover, EUR 4M balance sheet, energy | essential | Headcount alone exceeds the medium ceilings; a large Annex I entity is essential (Art. 3(1)(a)). |
| size-09 | DE | 10 employees, exactly EUR 10M turnover and EUR 10M balance sheet, manufacturing | out_of_scope | 'Does not exceed EUR 10 million' (Recommendation Annex Art. 2(2)): the boundary value stays small. |

| any-size-02 | DE | 5-person data-centre provider | out_of_scope | Same as cloud: an Annex I activity subject to the size test. |
| any-size-03 | DE | 5-person content delivery network provider | out_of_scope | Same as cloud: an Annex I activity subject to the size test. |
| any-size-04 | DE | 5-person DNS service provider | essential | Art. 2(2)(a)(iii): in scope regardless of size; Art. 3(1)(b): essential regardless of size. |
| any-size-05 | DE | 5-person top-level domain name registry | essential | Art. 2(2)(a)(iii) and Art. 3(1)(b). |
| any-size-06 | DE | 5-person qualified trust service provider | essential | Art. 2(2)(a)(ii) and Art. 3(1)(b). |

| any-size-09 | DE | 80-person public electronic communications provider, EUR 20M turnover, EUR 15M balance sheet | essential | A medium-sized provider of public electronic communications is essential (Art. 3(1)(c)). |

| si-05 | SI | 60 employees, EUR 50M turnover, EUR 10M balance sheet, energy | essential | Art. 7(2) pt 1 is disjunctive: at least 250 employees OR turnover of at least EUR 50M OR a balance sheet total of at least EUR 43M; EUR 50M alone suffices once the general test is met. |
